edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource (from Three Hundred Tang Poems).
edition.zh: 据维基文库（《唐诗三百首》本）。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died in 761.

note.en: From the Wangchuan Collection: Wang Wei wrote a quatrain on each of twenty places on his country estate, and his friend Pei Di answered every one. It is a poem about being unseen and not minding: no one knows he is there, and the moon comes anyway. The long whistle, 长啸, was an art of the recluse, somewhere between singing and breathing.
note.zh: 出自《辋川集》：王维为辋川别业的二十处景致各写一首绝句，好友裴迪一一唱和。这是一首关于不被看见而毫不介意的诗：没有人知道他在这里，月亮还是来了。“长啸”是隐士的一种技艺，介于歌唱与吐纳之间。

excerpt.orig: 深林人不知，明月來相照。
excerpt.en: Deep in the wood, no one knows I am here; / the bright moon comes to shine on me.
excerpt.zh: 深林人不知，明月来相照。

gloss.en: A dark, deep bamboo grove. The Bamboo Grove Lodge was one of the scenes on Wang Wei’s Wangchuan estate, in the hills south-east of Chang’an.
gloss.zh: 幽篁：幽深的竹林。竹里馆是王维辋川别业的一景。

gloss.en: The qin, a seven-stringed zither, the instrument of scholars.
gloss.zh: 琴：七弦琴，古代文人的乐器。

gloss.en: A long, clear whistling or chanting, a practice of recluses.
gloss.zh: 长啸：撮口发出悠长清越的声音，古代隐士常以此抒怀。
